strengths: Rejects ‘Japanese people never jaywalk’ as a daytime-station composite.
Separates Road Traffic Act from train manners; that contrast is culturally useful.
Flashing green as finish-don’t-begin on wide Tokyo crossings is accurate everyday teaching.
Waiting is not framed as unique Japanese soul or extra obedience.

issues.location: Empty Streets — ‘a camera sits on the pole’ / Learn to Stop — station cameras
issues.problem: Readers can take pole cameras as pedestrian-signal enforcement. Typical intersection cameras and station CCTV are not how most jaywalking is ticketed; being seen by people is the stronger local mechanism.
issues.suggestion: Keep ‘feeling watched.’ Treat cameras as possible, not a pedestrian red-light ticket machine. Do not invent camera-fine stats.

issues.location: Opening cluster including a bicycle rider
issues.problem: A bike waiting with walkers is common, but bikes are vehicles; the image can blur two legal categories before the later clarification.
issues.suggestion: The later bicycle paragraph already fixes this; optional: ‘a cyclist often waits with them anyway.’
